networks.label: Autobahn
networks.sign: Blue shield with a white number; the number also leads the blue direction signs

rules.text: Single digits are the long trunk routes: odd ones count up from west to east, even ones from north to south
Numbers in the 10s belong to the east: Berlin, Brandenburg, Mecklenburg, Saxony-Anhalt and Saxony
Numbers in the 20s belong to the north: Hamburg, Bremen, Schleswig-Holstein and the coasts
Numbers in the 30s belong to Lower Saxony and its edges: Osnabrück, Bielefeld, Hannover, Braunschweig
Numbers in the 40s belong to the Ruhr, the hills south of it and north Hesse
Numbers in the 50s belong to the Lower Rhine around Düsseldorf and Köln
Numbers in the 60s belong to the south-west: Rhine–Main, the Palatinate, the Eifel and Saarland
Numbers in the 70s belong to Thuringia, Franconia and west Saxony
Numbers in the 80s belong to Baden-Württemberg
Numbers in the 90s belong to the far south: southern Bavaria around München and the Swiss border
A ring around a city: it keeps its band but has no direction
An exception: its direction breaks the odd–even rule
